caption: One fixed event pair in two inertial frames related by v=0.6c. Components use metres, with time plotted as ct and signature +−−−. The squares are 5²−3²=4²−0²=16 m². The panels are coordinate descriptions, not two different physical histories.
alt: Two coordinate panels join red events A and B. The displacement is diagonal with components 5 and 3 in S, and vertical with components 4 and 0 in S prime.

caption: Endpoint worldlines of a rod whose rest length is 4 m, moving at 0.6c in S. A and B occur at ct=0 and measure 3.2 m in S. A and C satisfy ct′=0 and measure 4 m in S′. C has S coordinates (ct,x)=(3,5) m. Equal ct/x drawing scales are used; the right panel gives lengths in the respective measuring frames.
alt: Two slanted endpoint histories intersect a horizontal blue simultaneity slice at A and B and a rising gold primed slice at A and C. A side panel compares the rest and moving lengths.

caption: The same symmetric emission in the body’s rest frame S and in S′ moving at −0.6c relative to S. Each rest-frame pulse has energy L/2. The Doppler factors give left/right energies L/4 and L in S′, totalling 1.25L. The body has no recoil in S and hence unchanged velocity in either frame. Comparing its energy losses gives a kinetic-energy loss 0.25L; the text explains how the low-speed limit identifies the mass loss without assuming the body’s rest-energy formula.
alt: A body emits equal pulses to left and right in its rest frame. A second panel shows unequal Doppler-shifted pulse energies whose sum is larger. Ledgers compare total emitted energy L and 1.25L.
